clue.text: Priest who sounds like a beast

indicators.note: says the answer is spoken the same as a word for the animal that follows

blocks.note: the llama is a South American pack animal

explanation.surface: A clergyman whose name makes him seem like an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A lama is a Buddhist monk or spiritual teacher in Tibet, a priestly figure.

clue.text: Pianist, 4, at home cuddling cat with little energy

indicators.note: one thing cuddling another wraps its arms around it, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: being in means being at home
mog is British slang for a cat
E is the abbreviation for energy

explanation.surface: A pianist relaxing at home with a sleepy cat on their lap.
explanation.walkthrough: 4 is COOPER, so the pianist is Imogen Cooper; the cat and energy go inside IN to give IMOGEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Imogen Cooper is a celebrated British concert pianist, sharing the surname from 4.

clue.text: As one who sees things looking up?

definitions.text: As one who sees things looking up?

blocks.note: surface reading: someone with a hopeful, idealistic view of the world
setter's reading: literally gazing up at the night sky full of stars

explanation.surface: An optimist who always sees things improving.
explanation.definitionFit: Starry-eyed means naively idealistic, while literally suggesting eyes fixed on the stars overhead.

clue.text: Gosh – a funny trickster!

blocks.note: coo is a British exclamation of surprise
per means a, as in so much per head

explanation.surface: An exclamation of delight at a comic conjuror.
explanation.walkthrough: Tommy Cooper was a much-loved British comedian whose act was deliberately bungled magic tricks; the puzzle's other Coopers all refer back to this entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Tommy Cooper, the comedian in a fez, made his name as a magician whose tricks went comically wrong.

clue.text: Farmland's getting pouring rain south of Indian city

definitions.note: read as 'to do with farmland', an adjective

indicators.note: rain pouring down is tumbling about, so its letters are scattered into a new order
in a down clue, south of means placed below, so the second piece follows the first

blocks.note: Agra is the Indian city of the Taj Mahal
these four letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Fields getting soaked by a downpour south of an Indian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Agrarian describes things relating to cultivated land and farming, so it can stand for farmland's.

clue.text: Idiot in Conservative group

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
a lot is a group or batch

explanation.surface: A fool among the Tory party ranks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a container signal but here only joins definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Clot is informal British slang for a stupid person.

clue.text: 4's contribution to humour?

blocks.note: setter's reading: a cooper is a craftsman who makes casks, so his output is a cask of something
surface reading: what the comedian Tommy Cooper gave to comedy, a great deal of fun

explanation.surface: Praise for what the comic Tommy Cooper added to British comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: A cooper is a maker of wooden casks, so the trade and the comedian's name meet in one phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a very entertaining person or occasion, and a cooper's product is literally the container named.

clue.text: Rebuked youngster, learner expelled

indicators.note: someone expelled is thrown out, so that letter is removed from the word

blocks.note: a child is a youngster
L is the learner plate on a British car

explanation.surface: A young driver is told off and thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: Chid is the old past tense of chide.
explanation.definitionFit: To chide is to scold, and chid is its archaic past form, so it means rebuked.

clue.text: Spaceman got nr. Mars, going off course

indicators.note: something going off course wanders astray, so these letters stray from their order

blocks.note: nr. is the abbreviation of near, kept as two letters

explanation.surface: An astronaut reached the vicinity of Mars after drifting from his planned route.
explanation.definitionFit: Neil Armstrong was the astronaut who first walked on the Moon in 1969.

clue.text: In lake there is a fish

indicators.note: says one piece is placed inside the other

blocks.note: loch is the Scottish word for a lake
taken as written

explanation.surface: Somebody announces that a fish lives in the lake.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'a fish' together; the cryptic reading splits off the article to go inside the Scottish lake.
explanation.definitionFit: The loach is a small freshwater fish with barbels round its mouth.

clue.text: Herald in old city at end of month

indicators.note: placing something at the end of another puts it after, joining the two in sequence

blocks.note: AUG is the calendar abbreviation for August
Ur is the ancient Sumerian city

explanation.surface: A town crier in an ancient city at the close of a month.
explanation.definitionFit: To augur is to foreshadow or portend, just as to herald is to announce what is coming.

clue.text: Having a coat under the table

blocks.note: first meaning: covered with a layer of plaster
second meaning: so drunk as to have slid off one's chair

explanation.surface: Someone in their coat who has ended up beneath the table.
explanation.definitionFit: A wall that is plastered has a coating; plastered is also slang for very drunk, an idiom shared with under the table.

clue.text: Mister, one you caught as old forger?

indicators.note: something caught is held inside, so these pieces go within the other

blocks.note: MR is the abbreviation of Mister
taken as written
ye is the old form of you

explanation.surface: Asking a man whether he was arrested as a counterfeiter long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forger' suggests a counterfeiter, but here it means one who forges coins legitimately, a minter.
explanation.definitionFit: A moneyer was historically an official who struck coins, forging them in the metalworking sense.

clue.text: What I wear on head is rubbish!

blocks.note: first meaning: literally the headgear belonging to me
second meaning: an old exclamation of disbelief at something absurd

explanation.surface: Someone dismissing their own headgear as junk.
explanation.definitionFit: 'My hat!' is a dated exclamation of surprise or scorn, like saying nonsense, and also simply one's own cap.

clue.text: Lonesome artist retreating after short gibe?

indicators.note: something short is cut down, so the word loses its final letter
retreating means going backwards, so the word for an artist is read from right to left
says the artist piece comes after the gibe piece in sequence

blocks.note: an insult is a gibe or taunt
RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist

explanation.surface: A solitary painter withdrawing after a brief cutting remark.
explanation.definitionFit: Insular means isolated and inward-looking, close in sense to lonesome, cut off as on an island.

clue.text: Model needs encouragement, having wasted time

indicators.note: something wasted is lost, so that letter is taken away from the word

blocks.note: stimulation is encouragement or a spur
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A fashion model needs a pep talk after wasting hours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' reads as a person on the catwalk; it is the computer kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A simulation is a working imitation of a real system, as a computer model is.

clue.text: Regretting downfall: little good

blocks.note: ruin is a downfall
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Someone lamenting their collapse, which did them little good.
explanation.definitionFit: To rue is to regret, so ruing is the present participle meaning regretting.

clue.text: Lines by female boxer, 4

indicators.note: one thing by another sits next to it, so the two pieces join side by side

blocks.note: a hen is a female bird
RY is the abbreviation for railway, i.e. railway lines

explanation.surface: Insults traded with a woman fighter in the ring.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry Cooper was a British heavyweight boxing champion of the 1960s and 70s, famous for flooring Muhammad Ali.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Henry Cooper was a celebrated British heavyweight boxer, sharing the surname from 4.

clue.text: Drug problem, so sir can suffer

indicators.note: something made to suffer is knocked about, so these letters are battered into a new order

blocks.note: fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: Addressing a man about a drug habit that can make him suffer.
explanation.definitionFit: Narcosis is a state of stupor caused by a narcotic, a drug-induced condition.

clue.text: Face in sleep turning over

indicators.note: turning over flips something round, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: a nap is a short sleep

explanation.surface: Someone's face as they roll over in their sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Pan is informal slang for the face, as in deadpan.

clue.text: Quietly hang round, getting us to eat a piece of cake

indicators.note: the outer pieces eat the other, taking it inside them

blocks.note: p is piano, the musical marking for quietly
to hover is to hang about in one place
taken as written

explanation.surface: Lingering silently near the table, hoping to be given a slice of cake.
explanation.walkthrough: The first two pieces join and then take the third inside, straight after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A pushover is something very easy to do, just as a piece of cake is an idiom for an easy task.

clue.text: Type of outfit if tum is abnormal

indicators.note: something abnormal is out of its usual state, so these letters are out of their usual order

blocks.note: fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: Choosing a style of clothing if one's stomach is an odd shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Mufti is civilian clothing worn by someone usually in uniform, so it is a type of outfit.

clue.text: Violent speeches? I stared nastily

indicators.note: doing something nastily means doing it in a twisted way, so the letters are twisted

blocks.note: fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A listener glaring back at a series of angry rants.
explanation.definitionFit: A tirade is a long, angry, ranting speech, so tirades are violent speeches.

clue.text: It's said you will record fuel used in winter

indicators.note: something said is spoken, so the answer matches these words when spoken

blocks.note: you will contracts to you'll, and to record is to log

explanation.surface: Telling someone to note down their winter heating fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: A yule log is a large log traditionally burned on the hearth at Christmas, winter fuel.

clue.text: Labour MP, 4, reporting electronic check

indicators.note: reporting means telling by voice, so the answer matches what is spoken

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for electronic, and to vet is to check

explanation.surface: A Labour politician announcing results of a digital inspection.
explanation.definitionFit: Yvette Cooper is a senior Labour MP and cabinet minister, sharing the surname from 4.

clue.text: See 7
Gem picked up by 9?

blocks.note: first meaning: a pearly feldspar gemstone
second meaning: a rock from the lunar surface that the 9 astronaut could collect

explanation.surface: A precious stone discovered by an astronaut.
explanation.walkthrough: 9 is Neil Armstrong, so what he picked up on his walk was literally a stone from the Moon.
explanation.definitionFit: Moonstone is a milky, iridescent gemstone; the question mark flags the literal lunar-rock sense.

clue.text: What may sound like old law-maker's drink

indicators.note: says the answer, when spoken, matches the word for the people that follows

blocks.note: the Medes were an ancient people whose laws, with those of the Persians, could not be changed

explanation.surface: The favourite tipple of an ancient legislator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The law of the Medes and Persians' is a biblical byword for an unalterable rule.
explanation.definitionFit: Mead is an alcoholic drink brewed from fermented honey and water.

clue.text: Some fell by the wayside – biblical issue

blocks.note: first meaning: in the Parable of the Sower, some of what was sown fell by the wayside
second meaning: offspring, in the Bible's phrase 'Abraham and his ...'

explanation.surface: A scriptural question that some people gave up on.
explanation.definitionFit: In biblical language seed means descendants, and in the parable it is what the sower scatters.

clue.text: Support for Tory PM no longer

blocks.note: first meaning: a framework or surgical belt that holds something up
second meaning: Liz ..., Conservative prime minister for seven weeks in 2022

explanation.surface: Backing for a Conservative premier who is out of office.
explanation.definitionFit: A truss is a supporting frame or bandage, and Liz Truss is a former Conservative prime minister.

clue.text: It is heard in these brief periods

indicators.note: something heard is taken in by ear, so the answer matches the spoken word

blocks.note: it is old slang for sex appeal or sex itself

explanation.surface: Something audible in short stretches of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' looks like a mere pronoun; in crosswords it often stands for sex appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: Secs is the short form of seconds, which are brief periods of time.

clue.text: Singer, 4, caught in a deception

indicators.note: says one piece is placed inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written
a lie is a deception
c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A singer is exposed in a con.
explanation.definitionFit: Alice Cooper is an American shock-rock singer, sharing the surname from 4.

clue.text: Nothing in their cup, sadly, rich in nutrients

indicators.note: says the first piece is placed inside the words that follow
something going sadly goes wrong, so the letters are put wrongly in order

blocks.note: fodder, taken as written
O is nought, zero

explanation.surface: Their cup is sadly empty, yet something else is rich in nourishment.
explanation.definitionFit: Eutrophic describes a lake or river over-enriched with nutrients, so that algae flourish.
